source.repro: CPU columns: `pnpm bench:real` in ~/src/gmod/hclust (the 5.0.0 column is the same matrices through the v5.0.0 wasm, warm call). GPU column: `node browser-tests/probe-gpu-distance-matrix.ts N V` in products/jbrowse-web, headed system Chrome, upload and readback included. Idle machine: a run taken under a shared CPU came out 2 to 3x slower across the board and was discarded. JS column: the pure-JS implementation JBrowse shipped with before the wasm port, `@greenelab/hclust@0.0.1`'s exported `euclideanDistance` called in the same nested-map pattern its own `clusterData()` runs (src/hclust.js:54-61), timed in isolation so the O(n^3) agglomerative merge that follows it in `clusterData()` never runs -- one node process per (N, V), first call. Same-shape synthetic data (a sine function of the two indices), not the real dosage matrices: `euclideanDistance` is a branchless sum of squared differences with no data-dependent branch, so its cost is set by (N, V) alone.
source.notes: 1000 Genomes phase 3 chr22:20-21 Mb, 2504 samples, 22,383 phased sites, matrices built the way plugins/variants builds them (one column per ALT allele, 2/called dosage, site-mean imputation, one 0/1 row per haplotype in phased mode). 2019 MacBook Pro, i9-9980HK single threaded for the wasm, Radeon Pro 5300M for the kernel. The kernel is one thread per pair looping over V from global memory with no tiling, so the GPU column is a floor. Its result matched an f64 reference exactly on these integer-dosage matrices. A second GPU pass on the matrices `pnpm bench:real --dump` wrote (byte-identical input to the wasm) reproduced every cell within 8% under a load average of 8; the wasm arms of that same sitting ran 2 to 3.5x slow and were discarded, so the CPU columns remain the idle-machine runs. The JS column is a different machine (node 24, Linux) and a different day (2026-08-25); it establishes the pre-wasm baseline's order of magnitude, not a fifth arm of the idle-machine sitting above.
